blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is the only active volcano in India as well as the entire South Asian region.
Narcondam Island, located in the Andaman Sea, is classified as a dormant volcanic island.
The Deccan Traps were formed by large-scale flood basalt eruptions during the Late Cretaceous period around 66 million years ago.
Ancient and extinct volcanic structures in mainland India include Dhinodhar Hills (Gujarat), Dhosi Hill (Haryana), and Tosham Hills (Haryana).
Do not confuse Barren Island (Active) with Narcondam Island (Dormant); this distinction is a common trap in UPSC and State PSC exams.
Deccan Traps volcanism is associated with the Indian plate passing over the Réunion Hotspot during the Late Cretaceous period.
Barren Island lies along the tectonic boundary between the Indian and Burmese plates in the Andaman Sea.
